reconcile.note: Matthew Henry names the apparent self-contradiction directly and resolves it by treating the two verses as guidance for knowing when silence or speech fits a given fool.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells presses Proverbs 26:4 and 26:5 as flatly opposed commands—answer, then don't answer—sitting back-to-back in the same chapter.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: Don't answer a fool according to his folly, Lest you also be like him.
sides.verseText: Don't answer a fool according to his folly, Lest you also be like him.

sides.snippet: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own eyes.
